text:
For most modern MacBook Air models, a 30W–40W USB-C charger is enough for regular charging, while 70W or higher enables fast charging on supported models. The right wattage depends on which MacBook Air you have.

Recommended charger wattage

MacBook Air model

	

Recommended wattage




M4 (2025), 13-inch

	

30W or 35W




M5 (2026), 13-inch

	

40W (60W max)




MacBook Air, 2022–2024

	

30W, 35W, 67W or 70W, depending on configuration




MacBook Air, 2018–2021

	

30W

Source: Apple Support — Mac power adapters, Apple MacBook Air specifications.

What I'd buy

Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W USB-C Charger (2-pack)

$49.99

Listed price · verified October 21, 2026

A versatile option with two USB-C ports and one USB-A port. Its 65W output is suitable for a MacBook Air, although connecting multiple devices reduces the power available to the laptop.

Source: Dealectric product listing

My advice: If you want one charger that works well for everyday use and offers some flexibility, a reputable 45W–65W USB-C Power Delivery (USB-PD) charger is a good choice. For fast charging, choose 70W or higher if your model supports it.

One question: Which MacBook Air do you have — M1, M2, M3, M4, M5, or an older Intel model? I can narrow it down to the ideal wattage for your specific laptop.
